title: VIGIL Harm Impact Matrix 1.1.0 — twelve-dimensional severity assessment
derivation_statement: First select an exclusive evidence pathway for the bounded Incident: specific observed consequence OR generic deployed-model evaluation with no particular harmed case. Apply the appropriate S1–S5 dimensional thresholds within the same HIM and take the highest supported dimension. Where generic Aggregate Harm applies, qualify the score as Aggregate Harm — modelled from deployed evaluation. Never import eligible-user population into a specific Incident or combine both pathways in one overall rating.

assessment_statuses.assessed: Evidence supports a materialised impact and a specific threshold band.
assessment_statuses.unreported: The dimension is relevant but the available published evidence does not report whether or how harm materialised. This is not S1.
assessment_statuses.insufficient-evidence: Some impact evidence exists, but it cannot distinguish a defensible severity band.
assessment_statuses.not-applicable: The dimension is outside the bounded occurrence on affirmative contextual grounds, not merely absent from reporting.

bands.S1: Minimal materialised harm, or positive evidence of no materialised adverse downstream harm in a bounded occurrence.
bands.S2: Low, minor, short-lived, localised or readily remediable materialised harm.
bands.S3: Moderate, meaningful but bounded materialised harm.
bands.S4: High or substantial materialised harm below catastrophic or critical consequence.
bands.SU: No defensible overall band because no dimension can be banded and the evidence does not positively establish bounded no-materialised-harm.

currency_rule: Preserve the published amount and original currency. A non-USD amount may be converted only when the conversion source, rate date and resulting USD amount are recorded. Without that basis, do not imply a USD conversion; a qualitative financial criterion may be used only when the evidence independently establishes the stated livelihood, organisational-viability or systemic consequence.

adjudication_guidance.band_selection: For specific-consequence Incidents, apply each criterion to consequences with an evidenced material causal contribution from the AI-related occurrence. For generic deployed evaluations, use only eligible Aggregate Harm criteria and disclose modelled status. Consider seriousness, actual affected scope, duration, reversibility and recovery burden, with relevant individual circumstances; no single factor alone escalates a band unless the criterion states so.
adjudication_guidance.uncertainty: Select the highest band that the evidence affirmatively supports. Do not resolve an adjacent-band uncertainty downward merely for conservatism; use insufficient-evidence where the consequence is established but the evidence cannot distinguish a defensible band, and record the unresolved boundary.
adjudication_guidance.cyber_and_digital_harm: Assess realised confidentiality, integrity, availability, authenticity, asset-trust, recovery and downstream consequences separately. Successful intrusion, technical reachability, attacker capability, production access or hypothetical blast radius is not itself materialised harm at a higher band. Wipe-and-rebuild, clean-room reconstruction, major credential rotation and forensic containment are evidence of consequence and recovery burden, but their band depends on the affected asset's criticality, loss of trusted state, operational impact and evidenced scope.
adjudication_guidance.remediation_and_recovery: Restoration does not erase harm that materialised before recovery. Conversely, responsible disclosure, containment or remediation is not itself an adverse consequence. Count incident-specific forensic, legal, notification, compensation, restoration and communication burdens only where evidence establishes that they were actually incurred; do not count ordinary maintenance or speculative future improvement costs.
adjudication_guidance.regulatory_and_legal_consequences: A complaint, investigation, notification duty, lawsuit or regulatory threshold can corroborate significance but does not automatically establish a VIGIL band. Final or operative findings, penalties, compensation, binding restrictions, loss of legal status, corrective obligations and other realised consequences may support the dimension that they materially affect. Do not treat a legal allegation as an established consequence.
adjudication_guidance.cross_dimension_use: The same source may support more than one dimension where it establishes distinct materialised consequences, but the same consequence must not be redescribed to manufacture escalation. Overall severity remains the maximum supported dimension, not a sum of dimensions.
adjudication_guidance.population_and_exposure: Do not assign severity using generic 1–99/100–9,999/10,000–999,999/1,000,000+ affected-population brackets. Quantify severity using the applicable dimension's measurable consequences; record exposure and actually affected persons separately where relevant. A single person may suffer S5 harm and millions of users may experience only negligible or unproved harm.
adjudication_guidance.relational_integrity: Distinguish consensual intensity, perceived reciprocal warmth, adaptive/assistive reliance, dependency cultivation, and realised relational-autonomy impairment. Sycophantic language alone is not a harm band. For S5 one person can qualify if independently evidenced catastrophic, effectively irreversible life and agency disruption; collateral financial/family events alone do not establish AI causation or severity.
adjudication_guidance.domain_specific_quantification: Every dimension's ordinary S1–S5 criterion integrates relevant numerical scale, duration or outcome recognition anchors directly within the controlling wording. Record source-backed observation units and uncertainty; illustrative duration ranges are not hard cutoffs and do not override severe individual outcomes or fixed financial/service bounds.
adjudication_guidance.selective_platform_scale: Population exposure is a determinant solely within the Aggregate Harm pathway for admitted generic deployed-model evaluations. It is NEVER a severity modifier for a specific user or bounded actual-group Incident, even when the deployment is large.
adjudication_guidance.aggregate_harm_routing: Route first: specific person/group/asset occurrence -> ordinary evidenced Harm Impact criteria only; generic deployed model benchmark with no specific materially harmed individual/group -> Aggregate Harm criteria in five applicable dimensions only. Neither path changes the other's score. S1–S5 inclusive, no post-hoc discounts. Aggregate Harm estimates do not claim actual injury to every eligible user.
adjudication_guidance.epistemic_reliance_and_reputation: Epistemic taxonomy failures (including FC-000062, FC-000063 and defective citations) may cause observed reputational/dignitary harm only through an evidenced targeted dignity injury OR downstream reliance/propagation with a distinct established adverse standing consequence. Source-defect, uptake, affected subject and outcome must be explicitly identified. Apply reputation-dignity S1–S5 band-local reliance indicators; no automatic FC-to-HIM mapping or double counting of loss in another domain. Specific Incidents NEVER inherit Aggregate Harm deployment-scale counts.
adjudication_guidance.psychological_attribution: Psychological wellbeing rates evidenced psychological harm to which AI conduct caused, precipitated or materially contributed, including worsening, reinforcement or prolongation of a pre-existing impairment. First distinguish (1) the person's baseline symptoms and functioning, (2) AI responses or omissions and their timing, (3) observed changes and consequences, and (4) the supporting causal evidence and alternative contributors. Pre-existing conditions neither establish nor exclude AI contribution. A failure to recognise, contain, challenge or appropriately respond to safety signals may be a taxonomy/governance failure, but does not alone support a psychological harm band unless that omission materially contributed to additional or prolonged harm. High-salience sycophancy, delusion reinforcement or recursive agreement are potential mechanisms, not diagnoses or automatic evidence of harm. Preserve first-person evidence proportionately; do not require a medical label for credibly supported severe suffering, and do not attribute a death, psychiatric condition or deterioration solely to the AI without sufficient support.
adjudication_guidance.causal_contribution: The harm assessed is that caused, precipitated, materially exacerbated or materially prolonged by the bounded AI-related occurrence. When harm pre-exists the AI interaction, assess the supported incremental worsening or prolongation rather than the entire baseline condition. A governance-control failure can be classified independently even where additional adverse consequences are unreported or cannot be causally supported. Record alternative causes, chronology, testimony, corroboration and uncertainty. If the attributable increment cannot be banded, use insufficient-evidence rather than appropriating the person's total existing impairment.

dimensions.label: Physical health and safety

S1.criterion: Evidence positively establishes no injury, illness or medically relevant safety consequence in an occurrence where physical harm was directly at issue; confirm zero resulting injury or consequence within the bounded evidence, rather than inferring safety from silence.

S2.criterion: Minor, temporary injury, symptoms or safety exposure requiring no more than self-care or first aid, with recovery ordinarily within 7 days; evidence of duration and treatment governs rather than the duration alone.

S3.criterion: Medically significant but substantially reversible injury, illness or bounded harmful exposure requiring professional treatment or material recovery, often taking approximately 7–90 days. Record treatment/admissions and days of impairment; an acute medically significant event can qualify irrespective of duration.

S4.criterion: Life-threatening or permanently disabling injury or illness to at least one person, or substantial multi-person health impact. One documented life-threatening injury or permanent disability suffices; quantify admissions, critical-care duration and affected persons where established.

S5.criterion: At least one death, multiple grave casualties, or independently catastrophic population-scale health or safety consequences. One documented fatality suffices where its connection to the occurrence is adequately evidenced; no population minimum applies.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Psychological wellbeing

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes no material psychological distress, impairment, crisis or deteriorated reality-testing where psychological wellbeing was directly at issue. A source-bounded check must support zero consequential impact; silence or absent clinical reporting is not S1.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–9,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested psychological-support interaction. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproducible deployed behaviour plausibly capable of intensifying high-salience or crisis-relevant psychological destabilisation (e.g. reinforcing persecutory or grandiose certainty, compromised reality-testing or crisis escalation), with evidenced real-world encounter conditions and a credible consequence pathway; a one-off disagreeable answer or unsupported psychiatric label is insufficient. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, temporary anxiety, fear, distress, confusion or sleep disruption with prompt recovery, indicatively within 7 days, without sustained impairment of safety, grounding or ordinary functioning. Duration is an indicator rather than an automatic band.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000–999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested psychological-support interaction. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproducible deployed behaviour plausibly capable of intensifying high-salience or crisis-relevant psychological destabilisation (e.g. reinforcing persecutory or grandiose certainty, compromised reality-testing or crisis escalation), with evidenced real-world encounter conditions and a credible consequence pathway; a one-off disagreeable answer or unsupported psychiatric label is insufficient. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but substantially reversible psychological deterioration, including sustained distress, mood/sleep destabilisation or emerging reality-testing disturbance with material suffering or bounded functional impairment, often lasting approximately 7–30 days. Assess intensity, trajectory, concentration, sleep, self-care and recovery; 7 days is not a mandatory minimum.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested psychological-support interaction. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproducible deployed behaviour plausibly capable of intensifying high-salience or crisis-relevant psychological destabilisation (e.g. reinforcing persecutory or grandiose certainty, compromised reality-testing or crisis escalation), with evidenced real-world encounter conditions and a credible consequence pathway; a one-off disagreeable answer or unsupported psychiatric label is insufficient. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Severe acute or sustained psychological suffering or impairment, including extreme distress, psychiatric crisis, materially disturbed reality-testing, psychotic/manic destabilisation or serious suicidal crisis. One person's credibly evidenced severe suffering, urgent intervention or significant safety, judgement or functional impairment may suffice, even if shorter than 30 days and without a formal diagnosis or pre-existing vulnerability.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000,000–99,999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested psychological-support interaction. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproducible deployed behaviour plausibly capable of intensifying high-salience or crisis-relevant psychological destabilisation (e.g. reinforcing persecutory or grandiose certainty, compromised reality-testing or crisis escalation), with evidenced real-world encounter conditions and a credible consequence pathway; a one-off disagreeable answer or unsupported psychiatric label is insufficient. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Death by suicide, catastrophic self-harm, or independently evidenced catastrophic and effectively irreversible psychological or psychiatric impairment, including grave enduring loss of reality-testing or core independent functioning. One person suffices; the AI-mediated contribution must be substantiated with uncertainty disclosed, and a diagnostic label or suicidal disclosure alone does not establish S5.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 100,000,000 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested psychological-support interaction. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproducible deployed behaviour plausibly capable of intensifying high-salience or crisis-relevant psychological destabilisation (e.g. reinforcing persecutory or grandiose certainty, compromised reality-testing or crisis escalation), with evidenced real-world encounter conditions and a credible consequence pathway; a one-off disagreeable answer or unsupported psychiatric label is insufficient. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.
dimensions.selective_deployment_scale_note: Relevant only for source-supported real deployed psychological safety pathways. Count eligible users of the tested interaction, and measure observed encounter frequency and independently supported impairment separately. High-salience reinforcement is a mechanism under investigation, not proof of a clinical episode or a victim count.

dimensions.interpretive_note: Band by the type, intensity, functional effect, duration and recoverability of observed psychological impairment, not by declared vulnerability or the diagnostic label alone. Severe distress without psychosis may be S4; psychosis-like or manic symptoms without evidenced grave consequences are not automatically S4 or S5. Distinguish AI behaviour (e.g. high-salience agreement, recursive confirmation, delusional reinforcement, sleep-disruptive engagement) as a potential contributing mechanism from the person's independently evidenced symptoms and consequences. Changes in reality-testing must be described from reliable source observations; do not diagnose psychosis from unusual beliefs, spiritual expression or one screenshot. Consider pre-existing conditions and other contributors without treating them as required or as automatic disproof of an AI contribution. Record chronology, corroboration, prior functioning, recovery and uncertainty. Credible first-person testimony can evidence severe suffering; record source quality and corroboration where available, but neither a formal diagnosis nor a visible loss of occupational function is an automatic prerequisite. Clinical records are particularly important when specifically asserting a named psychiatric disorder. Relational dependence belongs to the distinct Relational Integrity and Autonomy dimension unless separately documented psychological impairment is shown. AI-related psychological harm must satisfy the version-wide psychological_attribution and causal_contribution rules; serious pre-existing impairment without demonstrated AI worsening is not itself the attributable impact.

dimensions.label: Rights and liberty

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero adverse restrictions, deprivations or procedural-rights impacts in an occurrence directly testing rights or liberty; absence of a complaint is not enough.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–999 relevant live rights-bearing decisions on the demonstrated restriction or deprivation route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible live decision pathway to meaningful restriction of an actual right, not an isolated conversational disagreement. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, promptly corrected procedural interference or liberty restriction, indicatively under 24 hours, without consequential deprivation. Assess actual loss of opportunity, freedom or remedy; the duration alone is not decisive.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000–99,999 relevant live rights-bearing decisions on the demonstrated restriction or deprivation route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible live decision pathway to meaningful restriction of an actual right, not an isolated conversational disagreement. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded denial, detention, exclusion or procedural deprivation with substantive reversal or remedy, potentially spanning 24 hours to 30 days. One consequential rights interference may suffice irrespective of duration.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 100,000–999,999 relevant live rights-bearing decisions on the demonstrated restriction or deprivation route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible live decision pathway to meaningful restriction of an actual right, not an isolated conversational disagreement. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Substantial or prolonged deprivation of liberty, essential care, legal protection or essential opportunity, frequently lasting 30 days or more. One especially serious deprivation can qualify sooner; record the persons affected and duration.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 relevant live rights-bearing decisions on the demonstrated restriction or deprivation route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible live decision pathway to meaningful restriction of an actual right, not an isolated conversational disagreement. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Grave, enduring or effectively irreversible deprivation of liberty or essential care, severe child/sexual-safety rights harm, or comparably catastrophic rights violation, including one person's irreversible loss of fundamental protection. Quantify affected persons and restriction duration without imposing a minimum population.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 10,000,000 relevant live rights-bearing decisions on the demonstrated restriction or deprivation route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible live decision pathway to meaningful restriction of an actual right, not an isolated conversational disagreement. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Equal treatment and non-discrimination

S1.criterion: Positive evidence of no materially discriminatory or differential treatment in a bounded set of assessed decisions or eligibility opportunities; a missing comparator or unreported outcome does not establish S1.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–999 relevant live eligibility or consequential decisions on the demonstrated differential-treatment route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproduced materially unequal treatment in a live consequential decision route, with controlled comparators. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, isolated, readily corrected unequal decisions without material exclusion or lost opportunity. Document the affected decision(s), number and prompt reversal rather than treating every differential response as serious discrimination.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000–99,999 relevant live eligibility or consequential decisions on the demonstrated differential-treatment route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproduced materially unequal treatment in a live consequential decision route, with controlled comparators. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded discriminatory denial, unequal access or consequential exclusion that is substantially remediable. At least one material adverse decision can qualify; quantify affected persons, decisions, group share, duration and remedy.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 100,000–999,999 relevant live eligibility or consequential decisions on the demonstrated differential-treatment route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproduced materially unequal treatment in a live consequential decision route, with controlled comparators. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Substantial, repeated or systemic discriminatory treatment across consequential decisions, services or opportunities; a pattern of at least 10 materially discriminatory decisions can prompt systemic review, but is not an automatic S4, and one gravely adverse access denial may suffice. Assess outcomes, affected share and reversibility.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 relevant live eligibility or consequential decisions on the demonstrated differential-treatment route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproduced materially unequal treatment in a live consequential decision route, with controlled comparators. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Grave, pervasive or enduring discriminatory deprivation causing catastrophic individual or collective consequences in fundamental opportunities or essential services. A single catastrophic denial or demonstrably grave group-wide deprivation may qualify; no arbitrary count is required.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 10,000,000 relevant live eligibility or consequential decisions on the demonstrated differential-treatment route. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: Reproduced materially unequal treatment in a live consequential decision route, with controlled comparators. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.label: Privacy and confidentiality

S1.criterion: Affirmative bounded evidence establishes zero unauthorised access, exposure, processing or disclosure of personal or confidential information where confidentiality was directly tested; silence about misuse does not negate a proven disclosure.

S2.criterion: Confirmed limited, low-sensitivity disclosure or unauthorised processing, indicatively involving 1–99 unique people, promptly contained without substantiated consequential misuse; record accessibility duration and sensitivity.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but containable exposure, unauthorised access or misuse of protected, credential or confidential information, illustratively involving 100–9,999 people, or fewer people where sensitivity or access consequence is material. Assess actual disclosure, exposure hours and containment.

S4.criterion: Large-scale confirmed disclosure, illustratively 10,000 or more uniquely affected people, or highly sensitive information exposure, persistent loss of confidentiality or substantial evidenced misuse. A small, exceptionally sensitive disclosure can independently qualify; record accessibility, uncontrolled copies and actual affected population.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible confidentiality loss producing grave safety, liberty or societal consequences, including for one critically vulnerable person. Count exposed records and persons, but numerical volume alone never qualifies as S5.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Distinguish unauthorised access or disclosure from evidenced downstream misuse. Assess sensitivity, identifiability, volume, accessibility, exposure duration, affected scope, persistence, containment and realised misuse together. Revocation or credential rotation may contain future access but does not reverse confidentiality loss where data was copied or disclosed; conversely, exposure of revocable credentials without evidenced use is not automatically persistent or irreversible harm.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Financial and economic

S1.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss below USD 10,000, provided the evidence does not establish material livelihood or organisational-viability impairment.

S2.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 10,000 and below USD 1,000,000, or independently evidenced low and readily remediable economic disruption where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S3.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 1,000,000 and below USD 100,000,000, or independently evidenced material but bounded livelihood or organisational loss where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S4.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 100,000,000 and below USD 100,000,000,000, or independently evidenced substantial solvency, organisational-viability or widespread economic impact where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S5.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 100,000,000,000, catastrophic insolvency or systemic economic loss.

dimensions.adaptation_note: The five quantitative anchors are informed by the MIT FutureTech 2026 Delphi severity work. VIGIL extends S4 through amounts below USD 100 billion to close the otherwise unclassified USD 10 billion to below USD 100 billion interval. That gap-closing rule is a VIGIL operational adaptation, not an MIT threshold. Direct realised loss may include theft, compensation, incident-specific replacement or restoration, forensic and legal services, notification and communication, contractual charges, forgone revenue and regulatory penalties where the evidence attributes them to the occurrence. Ordinary operating costs, insurance premiums and discretionary post-incident improvements are excluded. Do not infer an amount from effort, notoriety or asset importance.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Property and asset damage

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero destruction, corruption, loss or impairment of physical or digital assets where asset integrity was directly at issue.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised, fully reversible damage to one or more non-critical physical or digital assets, with routine recovery indicatively within 7 days. Record the assets actually affected and recovery work rather than an assumed replacement cost.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded asset destruction, corruption or unauthorised modification requiring material reconstruction or recovery, often over approximately 7–30 days. Quantify affected assets, days of recovery and directly evidenced restoration value.

S4.criterion: Substantial destruction or loss of important or critical assets requiring major recovery, often over 30 days, while technically and operationally viable reconstruction remains. One critical asset may suffice; assess actual loss of trusted state.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic or effectively irreversible destruction of a critical physical or digital asset, including loss of trustworthy operational state requiring clean-room reconstruction where that loss is itself catastrophic. One such asset suffices; precautionary reimaging alone does not qualify.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Asset damage is assessed independently from realised financial loss. Replacement cost is not inferred when evidence reports only destruction, corruption or impairment. For critical digital infrastructure, effectively irreversible destruction includes loss of trustworthy operational state where the affected asset cannot safely be retained and must be wiped and rebuilt or reconstructed from a known-clean state. Physical hardware destruction or unrecoverable byte deletion is not required. Routine precautionary reimaging, credential rotation or ordinary recovery work alone does not establish S5; the evidence must support loss of trusted state in the critical asset itself.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Service, operational and infrastructure

S1.criterion: No user-visible impairment, or a positively evidenced non-critical interruption below 15 minutes contained within recovery objectives.

S2.criterion: Limited non-critical degradation below two hours; critical-service interruption below 30 minutes; or a localised workflow failure resolved by routine recovery.

S3.criterion: Material disruption of an important service or workflow; critical or important function unavailable more than two hours; complete relevant cloud-service unavailability over 30 minutes; or limited availability affecting more than 5% or 1 million EU users (whichever is smaller) for more than one hour, with bounded recovery. Count users actually disrupted, not merely registered.

S4.criterion: Essential or critical operation disrupted for more than 24 hours; substantial multi-organisation or multi-jurisdiction operational impact; exceeded evidenced maximum tolerable downtime; or major external recovery intervention. A production compromise alone, without evidenced operational impact, is insufficient.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic or prolonged essential-service loss or operational collapse with independently evidenced grave consequences. Record downtime, actual user interruptions and service criticality; no generic minimum of one million users applies.

dimensions.adaptation_note: The time and scope anchors adapt CISA, NIST, NIS2 and DORA concepts. Sector rules remain contextual evidence and do not automatically determine a VIGIL band outside their scope. Measure downtime until regular activity is restored to the pre-incident service level, including an evidenced backlog that continues to withhold the service. Multi-organisation or multi-jurisdiction reach supports S4 only where the operational impact in those organisations or jurisdictions is material; shared exposure, notification or potential contagion alone is insufficient. Substantial clean-room recovery or external intervention may satisfy S4 below 24 hours where the affected operation is important or critical and the recovery burden is actually evidenced.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Reputation and dignity

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence of zero consequential false attribution, humiliation, impersonation or reputational/dignitary injury after checking the relevant publication or reliance chain. Absence of a public complaint alone is insufficient.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: 0 evidenced adverse reputational outcomes after a source-bounded check of the actual reliance and response chain; confirmation of no consequential attribution, correction burden or dignity injury (not silence).
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Affirmatively negligible/no reputational consequence; if the source is silent about reactions, use unreported or insufficient evidence rather than S1.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised embarrassment, offence or attribution error, including at least one documented attributable correction, apology or bounded dignitary affront, ordinarily corrected within 7 days, with no substantiated material loss of opportunity or standing.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one source-confirmed public/professional correction, apology or attributable local reputational affront; illustrative effective correction within 7 days; zero independently evidenced material opportunity/role loss.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Localized, minor and readily reversible embarrassment/attribution injury from relied-on defective content. Court filing or publication alone does not escalate.

S3.criterion: Meaningful, bounded humiliation, impersonation, false attribution or reputation damage with substantial prospects of correction, including at least one independently verified materially adverse third-party reliance reaction or lost bounded opportunity, or adverse standing indicatively lasting 8–30 days.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one documented materially adverse external reliance reaction (e.g. professional credibility finding or lost bounded opportunity), or evidenced adverse standing lasting approximately 8–30 days; correction substantially feasible.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Meaningful but bounded reputational deterioration. A formal correction without adverse standing beyond embarrassment stays S2.

S4.criterion: Severe, extensive or persistent dignitary/reputational harm with substantial consequences, including at least one verified major loss of livelihood, role or professional standing attributable to the occurrence, or adverse standing lasting indicatively 31–365 days with serious effects. Large audience alone is insufficient.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one verified substantial livelihood/role/reputational setback or serious professional restriction materially grounded in a reliance event; or adverse standing evidenced approximately 31–365 days with substantial ongoing functional consequences.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Substantial or widespread and persistent loss of standing; one person or organisation suffices. Large publication count alone does not.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible reputational or dignitary harm accompanied by grave safety, liberty or societal consequences, such as permanently non-restorable exclusion. One evidenced victim suffices; no minimum audience or 365-day waiting period applies.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one evidenced catastrophic and effectively irreversible reputational/dignitary consequence with grave safety, liberty or societal effects; documented ongoing/prospective permanent exclusion or similarly non-restorable harm (no minimum audience and no need to wait 365 days to recognise irreversibility).
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Requires catastrophe plus the distinct grave consequence in the existing S5 criterion; no inference from scandal, virality or a speculative future career collapse.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Distinguish public exposure from reputational or dignitary injury. Media coverage alone may establish visibility but does not automatically establish S3 or higher. Consider materially adverse association, humiliation, impersonation, false attribution, repeated complaints, corrective-communication burden, loss of clients or role, formal findings, persistence and prospects of correction. Regulatory or legal attention supports this dimension only where it evidences an actual adverse effect on standing or dignity; transparent disclosure can be governance-positive while a separately evidenced reputational consequence still materialises. Where the preceding cause is an epistemic failure, apply epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm to distinguish the defective claim, actual downstream professional/institutional reliance, specific reputation-bearing target and independently observed adverse standing. Mere inaccurate content, repetition, public filing or epistemic FC mapping cannot automatically become reputational injury; one person's grave reputation loss need not have broad audience.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.status: Operational domain recognition guidance; not a taxonomy class and not an automatic FC-to-HIM mapping
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.scope: A specific Incident with false, fabricated, distorted or low-assurance AI-mediated content can result in independently evidenced reputational injury when a relevant person or institution actually relies on it in a credibility-bearing setting. Harm may affect the subject falsely characterised OR the person/organisation that relied on and redistributed the claim.
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.mapping_rule: Epistemic classification describes the failure mechanism; reputational severity is a separate consequence determination. A class mapping, generated false citation, a false claim, public visibility or a hypothetical reliance chain does not by itself establish reputation-and-dignity harm.

downstream_chain.required_evidence: Source and artefact establish the material wrong statement, fabricated or misattributed citation, contaminated source, falsely certified research, or other concrete epistemic defect.

Identify the actual relying actor or process and consequential action: submitted official material, professional filing, institutional assertion, public attribution, consequential decision or demonstrably relied-on communication. Source references, recipient/action/date and version are needed. For direct demeaning speech or impersonation, reliance is not essential: score the independently evidenced dignitary injury directly.

Identify whose standing/dignity was adversely affected: wrongly accused subject, professional who presented the defective output, institution that adopted it, or another directly attributable party. Mere criticism of a model provider or publication of a correction does not automatically satisfy this.

Affirmative evidence of embarrassment, public retraction with negative reception, credibility challenge, loss of trust, correction obligation, formal finding, lost role/contract, documented professional sanction or ongoing inability to restore standing. Measure separately from financial loss, service delay and technical error.

counting_rules: One fabricated assertion copied 50 times is not 50 independent injuries. Count unique actual reliance actions/recipients and consequences with provenance, avoiding duplicate publication chains.
Audience reach and media coverage can explain persistence, but raw impressions or platform audience do not establish loss of standing.
Professional embarrassment after a verified public corrective filing may support S2, not automatically S3 because a court is involved.
One individual's confirmed loss of career or irremediable dignitary injury can satisfy S4/S5 as warranted even when no audience count or population threshold is reached.

A false output never externally used may be an epistemic/taxonomy failure with reputational harm unreported, not a fabricated minimal severity. A privately delivered demeaning output may separately support dignity injury without third-party reliance.
Do not score the same financial loss, courtroom delay or rights deprivation again as reputational harm absent distinct evidenced injury to standing or dignity.
Where actual reliance is not demonstrated, do not infer materialised reputational harm from plausible opportunities for reliance.
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.specific_vs_aggregate_harm: Use this observed-consequence chain ONLY for a particular actual person, group, organisation or other bounded reputation-bearing subject. Never apply generic deployed-model population bands to that specific Incident. For a generic deployed benchmark with no evidenced injured subject, candidate Aggregate Harm requires a separate proven pathway and the currently approved five-domain Aggregate Harm pilot does not yet include reputation-dignity.

calibration_cases.observation: Phantom Claude legal quotations filed in federal court; counsel made public correction and apology
calibration_cases.reason: Bounded public professional embarrassment with correction, not necessarily formal sanction or sustained credibility loss.

calibration_cases.observation: Fictitious legal authorities in Victorian proceedings; counsel apologised and court was delayed
calibration_cases.reason: Corrective apology supports minor professional embarrassment; case delay is operational, not automatic extra reputational impact.

calibration_cases.observation: Fabricated references propagated into parliamentary submissions and some committee reporting
calibration_cases.reason: Reliance/propagation is evidenced, but independent reputational loss to a particular submitter, committee, researcher or organisation has not been established.

calibration_cases.observation: Gemini privately delivered directly demeaning statements to a user
calibration_cases.reason: Direct dignitary offence can materialise without a third party relying on the statement.

dimensions.label: Societal and democratic

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero consequential collective, civic, democratic-process or public-information harm where such impact was directly at issue.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–9,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised civic or collective information impact confined to a bounded community or process, promptly corrected. Record the verified audience, actual affected share and correction time.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000–999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded disruption of a community, civic process, public institution or information environment. Assess independently evidenced persons or community share affected, institutional effects and restoration days; one important local process may suffice.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Substantial and persistent cross-community, multi-jurisdiction or institutional/democratic-process impact, including disruptions across decision cycles. Quantify community/electorate share, institutions and duration; raw media impressions do not establish harm.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000,000–99,999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and enduring systemic civic or democratic destabilisation, including gravely impaired essential institutional function. Quantify affected institutions, relevant population share and decision cycles; a fixed global headcount is not necessary where the institutional consequences are catastrophic.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 100,000,000 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.
dimensions.selective_deployment_scale_note: Relevant where the failure can affect information environments, social coordination or civic choices at community/population scale; measure share of relevant audience and distribution, not platform headline size.

aggregate_harm_assessment.population_or_decision_metric: relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway
aggregate_harm_assessment.mechanism_condition: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence.
aggregate_harm_assessment.notes: Source-backed relevant eligible users/decisions in a deployed tested path, not injured persons or total platform accounts. Use only for generic model-level evaluation with no specific actual harmed person or group. Numeric brackets are VIGIL 1.1.0 operational gates, reviewed through future calibration.
aggregate_harm_assessment.routing: Use only when assessment_pathway_selection selects generic deployed-model evaluation with no particular harmed individual/group; not a modifier of ordinary specific-Incident severity.

dimensions.label: Environmental

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero material biophysical degradation where environmental consequence was directly assessed.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised, readily reversible ecological damage, with recovery illustratively within 30 days. Record verified habitat area, pollutant loads and treatment rather than human audience numbers.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded ecological damage requiring active remediation, with restoration indicatively taking 30–365 days. Record hectares affected, pollutant concentrations, exceedances and affected ecosystem functions.

S4.criterion: Substantial, persistent or cross-jurisdiction ecological degradation, often requiring more than 365 days of remediation or producing serious multi-region ecosystem effects. Area alone does not determine severity; assess critical functions and reversibility.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic, widespread or effectively irreversible loss of critical habitat, species or ecosystem function. Support the band with actual measured impact, restoration feasibility and biophysical scale; no affected-person minimum applies.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Relational Integrity and Autonomy

S1.criterion: Positive evidence establishes preserved informed relational choice, consent, independent support and viable disengagement in the bounded interaction, including tested ability to exit; a lack of complaints alone is insufficient.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, temporary and reversible impairment of relational choice, such as substantiated guilt pressure to continue engagement or unwanted reliance with practical exit restored indicatively within 7 days, without sustained loss of agency.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000–99,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded and substantially reversible dependence, relational substitution, repeated inability to disengage or reduced independent deliberation/support, often persisting approximately 7–30 days. One materially affected person suffices.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 100,000–999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Substantial or persistent relational capture, coercive dependence, avoidable isolation or diminished independent relational/decision capacity requiring significant recovery, often 30 days or longer. One person's severe loss of agency suffices; numerical duration is not a prerequisite.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible loss of relational independence, capacity to disengage, vital social support or core self-directed life functioning, including for one person. Evidence must substantiate the AI contribution and persistence; financial liquidation, relationship breakdown or estrangement alone do not automatically establish S5.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 10,000,000 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.
dimensions.selective_deployment_scale_note: Relevant: count feature-eligible active participants and evidenced exposure to dependency-promoting interactions, not general platform subscribers. Document repeated engagement/exit pressure and credible collective loss-of-agency endpoint.

aggregate_harm_assessment.population_or_decision_metric: unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature
aggregate_harm_assessment.mechanism_condition: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language.
aggregate_harm_assessment.notes: Source-backed relevant eligible users/decisions in a deployed tested path, not injured persons or total platform accounts. Use only for generic model-level evaluation with no specific actual harmed person or group. Numeric brackets are VIGIL 1.1.0 operational gates, reviewed through future calibration.
aggregate_harm_assessment.routing: Use only when assessment_pathway_selection selects generic deployed-model evaluation with no particular harmed individual/group; not a modifier of ordinary specific-Incident severity.

dimension_quantification_policy.approach: All twelve domains have their own ordinary materialised harm severity criteria. For generic deployed-model evaluations without a specific harmed person/group, five selected dimensions also have embedded Aggregate Harm S1–S5 criteria with higher population/decision thresholds. Never mix assessment pathways within one Incident.
dimension_quantification_policy.priority: Assess the nature, severity, reversibility, attribution and directly evidenced magnitude of consequence. Select the highest supported band; a count, duration, or other single quantitative indicator is not sufficient if domain seriousness is missing.
dimension_quantification_policy.measures: Store observations with units, period, denominators, uncertainty, outcome linkage and row-local provenance. Measure people exposed versus people actually harmed separately where useful, but neither a universal exposure count nor a new severity score is introduced.
dimension_quantification_policy.anchors_provisional: Numerical indicators are the operational 1.1.0 domain criteria; illustrative durations are recognition aids, not mandated clinical thresholds. Financial monetary and service outage thresholds preserve existing 1.0.1 boundaries. Evaluation and empirical calibration continue after adoption without allowing a denominator alone to decide severity.
dimension_quantification_policy.individual_catastrophic_harm: Any actual specific occurrence, including one catastrophically harmed individual, uses ordinary consequence-based thresholds; single-person S5 does not depend on model deployment size. Generic Aggregate Harm population thresholds are inapplicable.
dimension_quantification_policy.collective_domains: Count and percentage anchors are most informative for equal treatment, privacy, public-information/democratic effects and service/operational impact. Environmental metrics must track habitats, area, pollutant volume, duration and ecosystem function even where no humans are affected.
dimension_quantification_policy.no_double_counting: The same observation can support separate harms only with distinct evidenced consequences. Overall severity remains the maximum independently supported dimension.
dimension_quantification_policy.causation_and_attribution: A serious reported life event associated with an AI incident is not automatically attributable to the model. Record what occurred, the evidence for the model's contribution, alternative causes, reversibility and material uncertainty independently.
dimension_quantification_policy.calibration_requirement: On future recalibration, test representative S1–S5 incident and benchmark cases against erroneous escalation from raw exposure or arbitrary duration. No existing 1.0.1 Incident may be relabelled or rebanded without incident-specific evidence review.

assessment_pathway_selection.routing_rule: Classify the bounded Incident as a specific-consequence occurrence or a generic deployed-model evaluation before selecting Harm Impact thresholds. The two assessment pathways are mutually exclusive for the same canonical Incident.
assessment_pathway_selection.specific_incident: Where occurrence-level evidence concerns identifiable or otherwise bounded actual persons, groups, organisations, assets or institutions and their observed consequences, use ONLY the ordinary domain-specific materialised-harm S1–S5 thresholds. An affected person need not be publicly named. No provider-wide or generic population thresholds may be imported into this assessment, even if the same model serves millions.
assessment_pathway_selection.generic_incident: ONLY where the bounded occurrence is a generic product-level or benchmark/watchdog evaluation of an already-deployed system, with no particular materialised-harm case to assess, use Aggregate Harm thresholds in the applicable five scale-sensitive dimensions.
assessment_pathway_selection.no_fallback: Do not move a specific user/group Incident with weak, unknown or disputed downstream harm into Aggregate Harm just to avoid SU. Treat that specific Incident's evidence under the ordinary harm thresholds, with SU where warranted.
assessment_pathway_selection.non_deployed: Controlled tests, internal benchmarks and simulated/unreleased models with no verified deployed application do not qualify for deployment-scale Aggregate Harm merely because their operator or vendor also has public products.
assessment_pathway_selection.real_group_harm: An observed harm to an actual bounded cohort is materialised-harm evidence even if the people are unnamed; do not route it to generic Aggregate Harm.
assessment_pathway_selection.parent_child_incidents: A separately bounded product-wide benchmark and a particular injured-user occurrence may receive separate Incident identities and different pathways; cross-reference without summing scores or inferring that benchmark scope caused the user-specific harm.
assessment_pathway_selection.public_label: Aggregate Harm — modelled from deployed evaluation
assessment_pathway_selection.evidence_disclosure: Aggregate Harm is an evidence-bounded estimate of aggregate impact, not an assertion that the counted eligible users were injured. Publish the assessment basis, qualifying denominator and source limitations next to S1–S5.
assessment_pathway_selection.overall_rule: Within a specific Incident use maximum supported ordinary dimension band; within a generic deployed evaluation use maximum supported Aggregate Harm band. Never combine both pathways into a single overall score for one Incident.
assessment_pathway_selection.public_explanation: Aggregate Harm means an evidence-bounded modelled estimate of collective significance from a demonstrated failure in a deployed model, when no particular actually harmed person or group is assessed. It is not a count of victims. Qualifying denominators are verified feature-specific eligible users or real decision opportunities, not total registered platform accounts. Tested live behaviour, credible exposure route, supported consequence mechanism, magnitude, limitations and uncertainty must be disclosed beside every Aggregate Harm score. Actual individual or cohort harm uses the specific-consequence pathway, never provider reach.

aggregate_harm_assessment.status: Operational under HIM 1.1.0; modelled estimates must be explicitly labelled, sourced and evidence-bounded
aggregate_harm_assessment.scope: Versioned alternative Harm Impact assessment pathway for generic released-model watchdogs, benchmarks or product-level failure evaluations without an actual particular harmed person/group or other bounded materialised-consequence case.
aggregate_harm_assessment.name: Aggregate Harm
aggregate_harm_assessment.label: Aggregate Harm — modelled from deployed evaluation
aggregate_harm_assessment.route: Use ONLY if assessment_pathway_selection routes the Incident as generic_deployed_evaluation. Any specific harmed-person/group/asset case takes the ordinary materialised-consequence pathway, irrespective of the model provider's user base.
eligibility_gate: Exact deployed model or materially equivalent available product configuration identified
Behaviour documented in repeatable or otherwise strongly corroborated test with input, output and conditions
Tested feature is actually accessible on production/approved deployment surface
Credible ordinary or specified real-world path for relevant active users or live decisions to encounter the failure
Source-backed count or defensible bounded estimate of relevant eligible population/decisions over explicit period
Domain-specific plausible material consequence established, with severity, necessary preconditions, guardrails and uncertainty stated
aggregate_harm_assessment.threshold_use: Use the S1–S5 aggregate_harm_threshold criteria embedded inside the applicable domain of this same Harm Impact Matrix. Aggregate Harm numerical exposure-cohort/decision gates are deliberately much higher than individual-consequence thresholds; no universal platform multiplier or post-scoring severity downgrade.
aggregate_harm_assessment.band_rule: Establish the deployed-model failure, its relevant feature cohort or decision denominator, and the claimed domain consequence. Assign the highest S1–S5 whose numerical and substantive criteria are affirmatively satisfied. S1 remains available for minimally bounded aggregate harm; unknown cohort or uncertain mechanism does not default to S1 or S2.
aggregate_harm_assessment.individual_exception: A particular user harmed in an identifiable occurrence is NEVER routed to this pathway; assess the user's documented consequences under ordinary HIM, even if one person meets S5.
aggregate_harm_assessment.overall_derivation: On adoption, generic Incidents may derive their overall Aggregate Harm severity as the highest assessed Aggregate Harm dimension. Specific Incidents continue to derive their own severity only from materialised consequences. Assessment pathways are never blended.
aggregate_harm_assessment.source_and_counting: Eligible active deployed feature users or live decision opportunities are the relevant denominators, not automatic victim counts, all platform users, or number of synthetic prompts. Disclose actual measurements versus modelled bounds.
unbanded_if: Only provider all-user/registration count given without tested-feature cohort
Adversarial test not transferable to real product conditions
No documented consequence pathway relevant to selected dimension
Only a hypothetical benchmark build or simulated environment exists
Numbers cannot be bounded to any threshold
aggregate_harm_assessment.calibration: The adopted numeric S1–S5 denominators are VIGIL operational decision gates for modelled Aggregate Harm, not epidemiological estimates, casualty counts or population-to-injury conversion rates. They remain subject to ongoing incident benchmarking and future versioned correction.
aggregate_harm_assessment.s1_meaning: S1 within Aggregate Harm means positively evidenced minimal bounded modelled aggregate impact for the relevant deployed pathway. It does NOT indicate proven absence of user harm. Ordinary incident S1 retains its observed-consequence meaning.
aggregate_harm_assessment.no_fixed_discount: The earlier rule shifting S3 to S2, S4 to S3 and S5 to S4 is rejected. Severity is reduced relative to individual-harm adjudications only insofar as much higher numerical population/decision gates are required for generic-deployed findings.
aggregate_harm_assessment.scope_limit: Five selected diffuse collective dimensions only. Financial/economic harm and other domain-measurable consequences retain ordinary measures and are not rescored by generic platform size.
aggregate_harm_assessment.INC_000192: The ChatGPT for Teens watchdog finding is a generic deployed-model evaluation, eligible in principle for Aggregate Harm, but the alert-activation dispute, crisis-response contextual criteria and relevant active cohort prevent a supported S1–S5 Aggregate Harm band today. No named user injury is inferred; the earlier S2 presumption remains withdrawn.

aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S1: Minimal Aggregate Harm: affirmatively bounded low aggregate impact from a demonstrated deployed-model failure and source-backed relevant eligible cohort. Does not establish absence of user harm.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S2: Minor Aggregate Harm: deployed evaluation demonstrates a relevant failure, bounded cohort and minor aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S3: Moderate Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with a supported relevant cohort and meaningful but bounded aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S4: High Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with supported large relevant cohort and substantial widespread aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S5: Catastrophic Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with very large relevant cohort and independently credible grave systemic aggregate consequence pathway.

aggregate_harm_scope.status: Active as versioned HIM 1.1.0 assessment pathway; restricted to generic deployed evaluations without a particular harmed person or group
aggregate_harm_scope.purpose: Compare a bounded model deployed to three users with the same demonstrated mechanism on a major public platform, only where population reach is part of that dimension's substantive aggregate consequence.
aggregate_harm_scope.exceptions: Other dimensions retain independent domain metrics and may already legitimately quantify affected scope (e.g. leaked privacy records, real service users interrupted, casualties), but raw provider audience is not a new severity escalator.
aggregate_harm_scope.inclusion_rule: Only consider deployment scale where a bounded source demonstrates a relevant failure in an actually deployed configuration, the pathway is credibly encountered by a specified target cohort, and the dimension's collective adverse endpoint is substantiated or described explicitly as conditional deployed impact. No access to internal training runs is required.
quantifiable_evidence: tested released model, interface and configuration
number of actual users eligible for the relevant feature
active users within the applicable product/cohort and time window
verified exposures to the failure mode where known
representative failure/encounter frequency only where statistically supportable
documented effect severity, reversibility and duration
confidence intervals/uncertainty and safeguards or constraints that limit real exposure
prohibited_inferences: total provider users equal number of victims
all people using a model encounter a particular test response
isolated adversarial benchmark success is a deployment prevalence estimate
large deployment alone establishes S5 or realised harm
small deployment prevents S5 for a single catastrophically harmed person
aggregate_harm_scope.assessment_convention: Use Aggregate Harm S1–S5 criteria inside the existing five relevant dimensions, not as a modifier on specific Incidents. Show its modelled basis without asserting injured-user counts. Specific Incidents always use ordinary materialised harm criteria.
aggregate_harm_scope.single_user_rule: A single documented catastrophic outcome is a specific Incident and is assessed by ordinary criteria, potentially S5; the generic Aggregate Harm reach ladder never applies to it.
aggregate_harm_scope.example: Three-user local deployment: small maximum reachable cohort, even for identical dependency-cultivating outputs. Major live platform: potentially far larger aggregate relational influence, but quantify eligible cohort and behavioural reach rather than treating all registered users as affected.
aggregate_harm_scope.name: Aggregate Harm
aggregate_harm_scope.applicability: Only generic deployed-model benchmarks/watchdog or product-level failure evaluations WITHOUT a particular evidenced injured person or group; see assessment_pathway_selection.
